title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a complex, multiplatform malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a complex, multiplatform malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It is known to grant remote access to the file system, provide terminal session capabilities, allow proxying connections to other infected servers, and utilize the payload-transfer.service for lateral movement.

**Scenario Objectives:**
1. Investigate suspicious services and files
2. Identify and contain command and control (C2) communications
3. Analyze lateral movement techniques

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Service
levels.content:
While monitoring the target system, you notice an unusual service running. Investigate this service to determine if it is related to the Kobalos malware.

**Hint:** Check the status of all services on the system.
levels.solution:
To investigate the suspicious service, you can use the following command:

`systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`

This will list all running services. Look for any unusual or unknown services. In this case, the suspicious service is named `OpenSSHserver`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services on the system.

levels.title: Identify C2 Communication
levels.content:
Examine network connections and logs to identify any suspicious outbound communications that may indicate command and control (C2) activity.

**Hint:** Check the network connections and logs for any unusual outbound connections.
levels.solution:
To identify C2 communication, you can use the following command:

`ss -tulnp | grep OpenSSHserver`

This will show the network connections and ports used by the OpenSSHserver service. Look for any unusual or unknown connections. In this case, the suspicious connection is using port `7070`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and logs for any unusual outbound connections.

levels.title: Analyze Lateral Movement
levels.content:
Investigate the lateral movement techniques used by the Kobalos malware. Identify any services or processes that facilitate the transfer of data between hosts.

**Hint:** Examine the systemd services and logs for any indications of lateral movement.
levels.solution:
To analyze lateral movement, you can use the following command:

`systemctl status payload-transfer.service`

This will show the status of the payload-transfer.service. Look for any unusual or unknown activities. In this case, the service facilitating lateral movement is named `payload-transfer.service`.
